messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: KV cache error-rate spike on runtime-pool-us-east-1 (alert id: a-7261). 5xx increasing, tail latency up. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache

Ryan O: Ack. I'm oncall. Pulling metrics and logs now. Which deploys around the window?

Maria G: We pushed a continuous-batching change at 02:12 UTC (deploy 2026-03-14-02:12-cb). It flips 'kv_cache.reuse' to true and changes key derivation to use seq_offset optimization.

Devon H: Seeing lots of malformed outputs in logs too — sequences reusing older KV entries. Example: request id=rn-11f logs show last_kv_seq=5420 but current_seq=21, followed by repeated older kv lookups.

Priya S: Customer Impact: CS flagged 2 paid accounts with garbled completions (conversation contexts leaked). Tickets created: CS-9871, CS-9872. Not yet escalated externally.

Tomas L: Hypothesis: kv_cache.reuse + seq_offset optimization accidentally uses per-worker shared KV without proper request namespacing -> cross-request leakage when worker handles multiple sequences. Could be off-by-one in seq_offset math.

Ryan O: Can we reproduce locally? Maria, can you drop the exact diff for the change?

Maria G: Pasted diff snippet:
```diff
- cache_key = (model_id, prefix_hash)
+ cache_key = (model_id, prefix_hash >> 4, seq_offset)
+ reuse_enabled = True
```
Also added a fast-path that bypasses copy-on-write for matched keys to avoid alloc overhead.

Devon H: That fast-path looks suspicious — bypassing COW without copy means buffers can be mutated across requests. If seq_offset calculation non-unique, two requests can map to same cache slice.

Ryan O: Immediate mitigation: disable reuse to stop cross-request reads. Maria, can you roll a hotfix to set reuse_enabled=false and revert the fast-path?

Maria G: Rolling hotfix now: `git revert cbe4123 && deploy rollback runtime-pool-us-east-1 --tag hotfix/kv-reuse-disable`

incident-bot: Deploy started: hotfix/kv-reuse-disable -> runtime-pool-us-east-1 (rollout id: r-8893)

Priya S: Noted. I'm telling CS to pause outbound customer notifications until we confirm rollback effect.

Tomas L: Also pushing a log-level increase to emit cache key namespace + seq_offset for a couple minutes to verify collisions: `KV_DEBUG_NAMESPACE=1`

Devon H: After toggling reuse=false on two hosts (canary), error-rate dropped from 6.2% -> 1.1% over 4m. Tail latency improved. Can we continue rollout?

Ryan O: Continue. But we need to ensure no data-corruption persisted. Are there any persisted artifacts (on-disk) that could carry stale kv?

Maria G: No persistent KV on disk — it's in-memory per-worker cache. Rebooting worker drains that. Rolling restart will clear states. Plan: complete hotfix rollout, then rolling-restart pool to flush caches.

Devon H: I'll coordinate restart. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-worker -n us-east-1 --selector=pool=runtime-pool-us-east-1` — stagger 60s between pods.

CS Bot: CS tickets updated: CS-9871 status -> investigating; CS-9872 status -> investigating. No public comms yet.

Ryan O: Customer impact assessment so far: approx 12k requests affected in window 02:12-02:28 UTC, primarily short-chat workloads with heavy cache reuse. Two paying customers saw context bleeding; we have session IDs and are preparing targeted outreach.

Priya S: Logged SLA impact projection: <1% of monthly requests for affected accounts; finance notified.

Tomas L: Root cause summary (preliminary): sequence namespace collision + disabled copy-on-write fast-path bug -> shared buffer reuse -> stale tokens returned for subsequent requests when worker reused cache slice. Repro steps added to infra/tests.

Maria G: Post-rollback status: rollout finished at 02:45 UTC, reuse_enabled=false across pool. Metrics stable. I'll prepare PR with safer key namespacing and mandatory copy-on-write for any reuse path.

Devon H: I'll run the fail-case unit test against the patch: create two fake requests with close seq offsets and assert no shared buffer.

Ryan O: Handoff: I'm oncall for another 20m. Devon will take post-deploy monitoring and be primary after 03:10 UTC. Please update the incident channel when you see any regressions.

Priya S: Postmortem owner: Maria G. Timeline to draft: 48 hours. Action items: (1) revert reuse_enabled default to false until verified (2) add automated invariant that cache key includes request_uuid (3) add canary test in CI that simulates interleaved sequences (4) add alert for sudden spike in cache reuse ratio.

Maria G: Adding item (5): improve rollout playbook to include KV-state flush step when changing cache semantics.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (monitoring ok for 30m). Please file postmortem and tag #eng-runtime #eng-ml #incidents.

Ryan O: Thanks everyone. Quick notes: keep CS notified, escalate if any customer shows new corruption. Maria, ping me when PR is ready for review.

Devon H: Oncall handoff completed to Devon H at 03:12 UTC.

Maria G: Uploaded preliminary revert PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/commit/cbe4123-revert. Will include detailed test cases.

Priya S: Closing update to CS tickets after rollback confirmation.

Tomas L: Follow-up engineering tasks scheduled. I'll own adding the invariant checks (ticket INFRA-3214).

Ryan O: Good work. Postmortem please include exact trace snippets showing wrong seq offsets + sample request ids.

Devon H: Will do. End of thread.
